headline: MI5 has opened an AI threat centre, and an OpenAI executive told a House of Commons committee he could not promise the incidents reported so far are the only ones.
score_reason: Pool score 6 lowered by 1: speech and hearing took place on 13 Oct 2026, before the window, and our 14 Oct edition carried the MI5 half.
importance_line: People in Britain and lawmakers are affected first, then AI labs, since OpenAI could not promise that no further incidents will emerge and MPs opened an inquiry, though the remark is one executive's answer and the inquiry has only begun.
summary: The Next Web reports, drawing on Politico Europe, the Guardian and Courthouse News, that Sir Ken McCallum, director general of MI5, Britain's domestic security service, announced a new AI Threat Assessment Centre on 13 Oct 2026, the day a House of Commons committee questioned executives from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind and Meta; Tom Duff Gordon, OpenAI's head of policy for Europe, the Middle East and Africa, told MPs "I cannot assure the committee or you, Chair, that that is it", and committee chair Liam Byrne announced a new inquiry into AI safety. This adds to our 14 Oct 2026 edition, which carried the Independent's report on McCallum's speech; the hearing, the OpenAI answer and the inquiry are new to us.
notes: Follow-up flagged by the curator (14 Oct pool, MI5). Events of 13 Oct, so older than the window; new facts for our desk are the hearing, the OpenAI answer and the inquiry.
